Three pairings that do both. Written 9 July 2026 Reading 1 min read Topics typography Small food brands live on crowded shelves. The type has to feel handmade enough to be trusted and clear enough to be found. After a dozen packaging projects, I keep coming back to three approaches. One grotesque, two weights The safest and often the best. A single sans serif in a regular and a medium weight, set large for the name and small for everything else. It is what we used for the coffee roaster, and it lets the colour of the bag do the talking. A serif name, a sans for the facts A warm serif for the product name, a plain sans for ingredients and weights. The contrast tells people which line to read first, which matters more on a jar than anywhere else.
